title: Bounded northern and central European Latin missal book states

traditions.label: Nidaros provincial missal
traditions.scope: The printed 1519 Nidaros-use missal commissioned for the metropolitan province; Iceland and the Faroes are within the stated intended territory.
traditions.coverage_note: The edited print and its foreword establish the book and intended scope, but do not establish uniform local reception or a collated transition from earlier Nidaros books.

traditions.label: Turku diocesan Missale Aboense
traditions.scope: The 1488 Lübeck-printed Missale Aboense and its diocesan preface and calendar.
traditions.coverage_note: The National Library describes a composite parchment copy; print date and local components are identified, but original leaves and other copies are uncollated.

traditions.label: Zagreb diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Venetian 1511 Missale Zagrabiense bearing a title that reports diocesan synod and chapter approval under Bishop Luke.
traditions.coverage_note: The title and contents are transcribed in a scholarly catalogue. The original synod act, exact effective date, and later Zagreb cathedral and Jesuit routes are unresolved.

traditions.label: Roman-Bohemian missal
traditions.scope: The 1690 Roman-based missal printed at the Prague archiepiscopal seminary with Bohemian saints' proper Masses named on its title.
traditions.coverage_note: A digitized-book title transcription identifies the edition. Papal concession documents, original title image, complete propers, and reception remain uninspected. This is not assigned as a successor to the medieval Prague-use core.

traditions.label: Halberstadt diocesan missal
traditions.scope: Printed missals for the diocese of Halberstadt issued under Archbishop Ernst of Magdeburg as administrator: the c. 1498 edition with his mandate and the 1511 edition.
traditions.coverage_note: Mandate, title, colophon and January calendars are inspected in BSB copies; Mass bodies, other months and local reception remain uncollated.

traditions.label: Lübeck diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The Missale Lubicense catalogued for about 1505.
traditions.coverage_note: No original copy was located online; catalogue witness only.

traditions.label: Merseburg diocesan missal
traditions.coverage_note: No original copy was located online; catalogue witness only.

sources.title: Missale Nidrosiense, edited transcription and introduction, Bokselskap
sources.inspection: The edited opening title, printer's foreword and calendar, with the companion introduction's content survey and colophon report, were read on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: A modern edited transcription, not an independent collation of the original print or its surviving copies; the transcription itself does not establish province-wide actual use.

sources.title: Espen Karlsen and Sigurd Hareide, The Nidaros Missal (1519)
sources.inspection: Introduction sections on commissioning, print completion, province, contents and final colophon inspected on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: The account distinguishes intent from reception and notes rites absent from the missal; it is not a complete before-and-after liturgical collation.

sources.title: National Library of Finland, Missale Aboense (parchment composite) catalogue
sources.inspection: Holding-library record read on 2026-10-20, especially imprint, local preface and calendar description, composite-copy warning, and dated Bitz preface.
sources.limitations: The linked 330 MB original-image PDF was not acquired; exact leaf readings, the physical completeness of copies, and their relation to Dominican material remain unverified.

sources.title: Usuarium, Missale Zagrabiense, Book 92
sources.inspection: Catalogue title, 1511 date, OSZK shelfmark, and contents entries for calendar, Mass cycles, ordinary, Canon and rubrics inspected on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: The linked original-book PDF returned 401 in this research session. Synod and chapter approval are claims in the transcribed title; the original act, adoption and source-text differences were not checked.

sources.title: Missale Romano-Bohemicum (Prague, 1690), digitized-book title listing
sources.inspection: Long title and 1690 archiepiscopal-seminary imprint read from the digitized-book listing on 2026-10-20.
sources.limitations: The original title image and body were not inspected; title language concerning pontifical concessions and the archbishop's mandate is not the underlying acts or local use evidence.

sources.title: National Library of Finland, Missale Aboense parchment composite, Doria PDF fv31282_pergamenttikooste.pdf
sources.inspection: Whole 540-page PDF (330,077,146 bytes) acquired 2026-10-21; pp. 1–24 surveyed and pp. 6 (computus table), 7 (January), 12 (June), 18 (December) and 19 (holy-water ordo) viewed.
sources.limitations: A composite of leaves from several copies; the Bitz preface leaf was not found in pp. 1–24. Only selected calendar months were read.

sources.title: Missale Halberstatense with the mandate of Ernst of Saxony, [Strasbourg: Johann Grüninger for Peter Drach, ca. 1498], BSB 2 Inc.s.a. 879 f (MDZ bsb00032887; GW M24400)
sources.inspection: Canvases 1–24 surveyed as thumbnails; canvas 7 (printed mandate) and canvas 8 (January calendar) read at full size, 2026-10-22. The mandate of Ernst, archbishop of Magdeburg and administrator of the church of Halberstadt, to the clergy of the city and diocese of Halberstadt says that the missals in use vary among themselves and depart from the true rubric, and that he has therefore granted missals to be printed according to the order and true rubric of Halberstadt from the most corrected exemplars, urging churches to buy them; it ends 'Datum Halberstadt' without a date. Calendar canvases 8–19.
sources.limitations: No colophon was read; the date ca. 1498 and the printer are the BSB/GW attribution (the BSB note also cites Fuchs ca. 1493–1500, BM STC 1500? and Proctor's sixteenth-century placing). Body uncollated.

sources.title: Missale celeberrimi Halberstattensis episcopatus, [Speyer], 1511, BSB 2 Liturg. 223 (MDZ bsb00017961; VD16 M 5577)
sources.inspection: Canvases 1–24 and 520–543 surveyed as thumbnails; canvas 5 (title), canvas 7 (January calendar) and canvas 534 (address Ad clerum Halberstattensem) read at full size, 2026-10-22. The red title calls the book the missal of the most celebrated Halberstadt bishopric, carefully corrected at the instance of the clergy and printed in more pleasing type; the closing address praises Archbishop Ernst of Magdeburg under Pope Julius II and Emperor Maximilian and dates the corrected printing to the year 1511 ('millesimum quingentesimum undecimo'). A second MDZ object, bsb10942166, describes the same BSB copy.
sources.limitations: Printer and place are catalogue attributions; Mass bodies and other calendar months are uncollated.

sources.title: USUARIUM 7238 (Missale Lubicense) and 7271 (Missale Merseburgense) book records
sources.inspection: Both records read 2026-10-22: 7238 Lübeck, age 'about 1505', Amiet 543, USTC 741258 (more copies USTC 676212); 7271 Merseburg, age 1502, original-title incipit 'Ex quo missalium diversitas in dioecesi Merszburgensi ...', UB Leipzig III/243, Amiet 591.
sources.limitations: Catalogue metadata only; no original page seen.

sources.title: Karel Pazour, 'Zkušenosti ze správy duchovní: 1. Potřeba doplňků v starších misálech', Pastýř duchovní (1881), printed p. 382 (Czech National Library Kramerius)
sources.inspection: Page image (printed p. 382) acquired and read 2026-10-22 after a Kramerius full-text search for 'missale romano bohemicum': a parish priest reports that the rubric placing the Trinity preface on Sundays without a proper preface, by Clement XIII's bull of 3 January 1759, is printed in his missal of 1869 but is ignored by the 'Missale Romano-Bohemicum' issued in 1845, which he calls doubtless the most widespread missal in Bohemia; he also lists later additions (St Joseph in the A cunctis prayer, 1871) to be entered by hand.
sources.limitations: A contemporary practitioner's remark in a pastoral column ('Zkušenosti ze správy duchovní'), not a bibliographic description and not an inspection of the 1845 book by this project; the claim concerns one rubric. Publisher, imprint and approval of the 1845 edition are not stated.

stages.label: Printed Nidaros provincial missal
stages.scope: Printed Mass book's foreword, calendar, temporal, Order and Canon of Mass, sanctoral, commons, votives, sequences and accident rubrics as bounded by the edited copy's contents.
stages.summary: Archbishop Erik Valkendorf commissioned a corrected and augmented missal following the Nidaros metropolitan rite because older missals were scarce or defective. The print foreword states a goal of common celebration across his diocese and province; the edited colophon dates printing to 25 May 1519.

evidence.locus: part 1, opening title and printer's foreword, numbered paragraphs 1–2
evidence.claim: The book names Nidaros use, Archbishop Valkendorf's commission and a province-wide standardization intention.

evidence.locus: The Nidaros missal, first book printed on Norwegian initiative, paragraphs 3–5; content section, contents through colophon
evidence.claim: The authors identify the 25 May 1519 print completion and bounded missal components, including an Order/Canon, propers, calendar and rubrics.

stages.limitations: The original print and pre-1519 witnesses have not been collated against the edited transcription; no exact new prayer or rubric is identified here. The missal excludes some processions and blessings supplied by other Nidaros books.
stages.reception: The source establishes provincial intent, including Iceland and the Faroes, but no local adoption date or uniform observance there.

stages.label: Turku diocesan Missale Aboense
stages.date_label: 1488 printing after the 17 August bishop's preface
stages.scope: Local preface and saints' calendar in a diocesan missal printed at Lübeck; only the calendar is counted as a demonstrated local liturgical component.
stages.witness_label: Missale Aboense, 1488 print represented by the National Library parchment composite
stages.summary: The National Library identifies the Lübeck 1488 Missale Aboense for the Diocese of Turku, with Bishop Konrad Bitz's preface dated 17 August 1488 and a local saints' calendar. The surviving parchment object is assembled from fragments of multiple copies.

evidence.locus: Finna record, imprint and description paragraphs beginning 'MISSALE ABOENSE' and 'Esipuhe ja alkuun liitetty'
evidence.claim: Identifies the diocesan destination, 1488 Lübeck print, dated bishop's preface, and Finnish local calendar.

evidence.locus: Doria PDF pp. 7, 12 and 18 (January, June, December calendar)
evidence.claim: The printed calendar marks Henry bishop (20 January) and the Translation of Henry (18 June) as totum duplex, with Knut king (7 January), Eskil martyr (12 June), a church dedication (17 June) and Anne mother of Mary (9 December) as local entries.

stages.limitations: 17 August is a prefatory date, not the print or use date. Only the January, June and December calendar pages were read in the composite copy; other Mass components are uncollated. Fragmentary and composite copies cannot be treated as a single physically complete witness.
stages.reception: The book's intended Turku diocesan destination is documented by the holding library; individual parish use is not dated.

stages.label: 1511 Zagreb diocesan missal
stages.scope: Catalogue-attested diocesan missal with calendar, temporal and sanctoral Masses, ordinary, Canon and rubrics; the title reports a diocesan synod and chapter approval.
stages.witness_label: Missale Zagrabiense, Venetian print of 1511, OSZK RMK III 0176
stages.summary: The Usuarium catalogue identifies a 1511 missal according to Zagreb's choir and rubrics; its transcribed title reports confirmation and approval in a diocesan synod and general chapter under Bishop Luke. The contents inventory identifies the major Mass components.

evidence.locus: Book 92, Original title, Age, Printer and Shelfmark fields; Contents rows 3, 8, 281, 603–648
evidence.claim: The catalogue locates an exact 1511 print and transcribes the reported synod/chapter approval and Mass components.

stages.limitations: The transcribed title does not supply the original synod record, its date, legal reach, first use, or an exact comparison with medieval Zagreb manuscripts. No 1788 universal switch or parentage is inferred.
stages.reception: Diocesan destination and approval language are title-level attestations; actual use by a particular cathedral, parish or Jesuit house is not established here.

stages.label: 1690 Roman-Bohemian missal
stages.scope: Roman Missal book state whose long title advertises Bohemian saint Mass propers and pontifically conceded Masses under Archbishop Waldstein's mandate.
stages.summary: A 1690 digitized-book title identifies a Roman-based missal with Bohemian local Mass propers, including texts described as pontifically conceded, issued by command of Archbishop Johann Friedrich of Waldstein.

evidence.locus: Google Play Books listing, long title and imprint lines
evidence.claim: The title and imprint identify the 1690 Roman-Bohemian book and its stated local-proper and mandate scope.

stages.limitations: The original title and body, each concession, calendar, diocesan adoption and relation to the 1735 printing remain unchecked; the 1690 print is not made a descendant of the medieval Prague-use core.
stages.reception: A named archiepiscopal mandate on the title is not proof of reception at every Bohemian church or a first effective date.

stages.label: 1845 Missale Romano-Bohemicum as described in 1881
stages.date_label: 1845 issue reported by Pazour (1881); title and imprint uninspected
stages.scope: One rubric state of the 1845 Romano-Bohemian missal, as described by a Bohemian parish priest in 1881.
stages.witness_label: 1845 Missale Romano-Bohemicum, known from Pastýř duchovní 1881, p. 382
stages.summary: Pazour reports that the 1845 Missale Romano-Bohemicum, then the most widespread missal in Bohemia, does not carry the rubric, based on Clement XIII's bull of 3 January 1759, that assigns the Trinity preface to Sundays without a proper preface, whereas his 1869 missal prints it.

evidence.locus: Pastýř duchovní 1881, printed p. 382, section 1, paragraphs 2–3
evidence.claim: The 1845 Missale Romano-Bohemicum lacks the 1759 Sunday Trinity-preface rubric and was widely used in Bohemia.

stages.limitations: Provisional after cold review (2026-10-22): the only evidence is a parish priest's passing remark in a pastoral column about one rubric, not a bibliographic or liturgical-historical description of the book, so it does not meet the scholarly-description standard for a documented book state; the edition's title page, imprint, publisher and approval are unidentified. Known only from a later description of one rubric; the book's title page, imprint, approval and the rest of its contents are uninspected, and its relation to the 1690 and 1735 editions is not established. The absence is the author's report, not this project's check.
stages.reception: Described in 1881 as the most widespread missal in Bohemia; no dated adoption.

stages.label: Missale Halberstatense with Archbishop Ernst's mandate
stages.scope: A printed Halberstadt diocesan missal with its prefatory mandate and calendar.
stages.witness_label: BSB 2 Inc.s.a. 879 f (MDZ bsb00032887; USUARIUM 5818; Google Books xhKLX-OS2c0C)
stages.summary: The administrator of Halberstadt, Archbishop Ernst of Magdeburg, prefaces the book with a mandate that justifies a printed missal by the divergence and corruption of the diocese's manuscript missals and orders it to follow the order and rubric of Halberstadt; the calendar follows.

evidence.claim: Mandate identifying the diocese, the authority and the reason for printing; Halberstadt calendar.

stages.limitations: The date bounds 1493–1500 record the incunable-catalogue attributions (BSB ca. 1498; Fuchs ca. 1493–1500; BM STC 1500?), not an inspected colophon; the same BSB note records Proctor's sixteenth-century placing (BMC III p. 861), so the 1500 upper bound is not secure. The mandate is undated. Mass bodies are uncollated.
stages.reception: The mandate urges every church of the diocese to acquire the book; actual uptake is undated.

stages.label: Missale celeberrimi Halberstattensis episcopatus
stages.scope: A corrected Halberstadt diocesan missal printed under Archbishop Ernst.
stages.witness_label: BSB 2 Liturg. 223 (MDZ bsb00017961 / bsb10942166; VD16 M 5577)
stages.summary: The title presents the book as carefully corrected at the clergy's instance and newly printed; the closing address to the Halberstadt clergy dates the corrected printing to 1511 under Archbishop Ernst. Its January calendar agrees with that of the c. 1498 edition in feasts, grades and rubrics.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00017961 canvases 5 (title), 7 (January calendar) and 534 (Ad clerum Halberstattensem)
evidence.claim: Title, dated closing address and calendar of the 1511 edition.
The c. 1498 January calendar, compared entry by entry with the 1511 page: same feasts, grades and octave rubrics.

stages.limitations: The title's claim of correction is not shown to change content: the only compared page (January) agrees with the earlier edition, so no transition is drawn. Other months and Mass bodies are uncollated.
stages.reception: Addressed to the Halberstadt clergy; first use undated.

gaps.missing: Direct collation of the 1519 print with earlier Nidaros Mass witnesses and province-by-province or parish use evidence.
gaps.next_source: Original 1519 print images and local inventories from Norway, Iceland and the Faroes; pre-1519 Nidaros ordo and missal fragments.
gaps.consequence: Publication is documented, but substantive predecessor changes and uniform provincial adoption cannot be dated.

gaps.missing: January, June and December calendar pages of the National Library composite are read; pp. 25–540 were thumbnailed on 2026-10-22 without finding the Bitz preface leaf. They include the Canon woodcut (p. 300) and photographic facsimile leaves (about pp. 290–291, 301–302 and 311–312, the Te igitur on p. 301 numbered 249) whose source copy is unidentified. Remaining calendar months, Mass components, other copies and actual Turku use dates remain.
gaps.next_source: Identification of the facsimile leaves' source copy; the Copenhagen parchment copy and paper copies listed by the National Library for the Bitz preface; remaining months at pp. 8–11 and 13–17 of the Doria composite.
gaps.consequence: The diocesan book and local calendar are identified, but a full distinctive version and uptake cannot be reconstructed.

gaps.missing: The original synod and chapter act, source-text comparisons, exact diocesan reception and separate cathedral and Jesuit lines.
gaps.next_source: OSZK RMK III 0176 original book; Zagreb synod act; local directories and cathedral records.
gaps.consequence: The title's approval report cannot establish an act-history transition or a single later diocese-wide switch.

gaps.missing: Original printed title and propers of 1690, separate concession acts, local use and comparison with 1735, 1845 and medieval Prague materials. Batch 5 adds an 1845 edition known from Pazour (1881, p. 382) by one rubric, as a provisional stage after cold review; no Romano-Bohemicum title was found by title search in Kramerius (2026-10-22).
gaps.next_source: National Library of the Czech Republic digitized 1690, 1735 and 1845 copies (Kramerius, Manuscriptorium) and original archiepiscopal decree or approbation leaves; Pastýř duchovní and Časopis katolického duchovenstva for further descriptions.
gaps.consequence: The Roman-local book state is identifiable, but neither its exact prayer variants nor historical parentage is established.

gaps.missing: Only the January calendars of the two Halberstadt editions are compared (no difference); the other months, the Mass bodies, the c. 1498 colophon and the 1511 title's claimed corrections are uncollated; earlier manuscripts and later editions are unlocated.
gaps.next_source: MDZ bsb00032887 calendar canvases 9–19 and Mass sections against bsb00017961 canvases 8–18 and matching sections; final leaves of bsb00032887 for a colophon.
gaps.consequence: Two documented Halberstadt book states with no established textual difference.

gaps.missing: No original copy of the Missale Lubicense was found online (MDZ metadata search, web search, 2026-10-22; the Google Books API refused with a quota error); title, colophon, date and contents are known only from USUARIUM 7238 and its Amiet and USTC references.
gaps.next_source: USTC 741258 and 676212 copy lists; Stadtbibliothek Lübeck and Kiel/Rostock holdings; GW/VD16 entries for Lübeck missals.
gaps.consequence: The route has no Lübeck stage; the catalogue witness stays a candidate.

gaps.missing: No digitised copy of the Missale Merseburgense was found (MDZ metadata search, web search, 2026-10-22). USUARIUM 7271 cites UB Leipzig III/243 and a title beginning 'Ex quo missalium diversitas in dioecesi Merszburgensi', which suggests a mandate on divergent missals; neither has been seen.
gaps.next_source: UB Leipzig III/243 (Leipzig digital collections); VD16 entry for the 1502 Merseburg missal; Merseburg cathedral library holdings.
gaps.consequence: The route has no Merseburg stage; the catalogue witness stays a candidate.
